investment_thesis.summary: MUFG is the flagship beneficiary of the structural normalization in Japanese interest rates. With the BOJ hiking policy rates to 1.25% on September 18, 2026, MUFG's domestic retail deposit base (>¥220 trillion, deposit beta <8%) generates immediate pre-tax net interest income expansion of ~¥70 billion per 25 bps. Trading at an unjustified 0.98x P/B with an 11.3% ROE, its cash flows are further insulated by its 22% stake in Morgan Stanley and sustained annual buybacks exceeding ¥400 billion.
return_engines: Engine 1: Domestic NIM expansion (+¥70B pre-tax per 25 bps hike) on sticky ¥220T deposit base
Engine 2: Strategic overseas equity dividends and advisory profits from Morgan Stanley
Engine 3: Systematic share repurchases (>¥400B annually) and progressive dividend resets (3.6% yield)
market_implied_assumptions: Terminal BOJ policy rate plateaus at 1.25% with no further tightening
Domestic credit costs rise sharply among SME borrowers as rates rise
why_price_may_differ_from_value: Market underestimates the extreme stickiness of Japanese retail deposits, resulting in peak NIMs far exceeding historical assumptions
Persistent deflationary discounting suppresses the valuation multiple below 1.0x P/B despite ROE consistently exceeding 11.0%

decision.summary: MUFG is the undisputed anchor of the JPY structural thesis. Trading at 0.98x P/B with an 11.3% ROE, it offers double-digit upside to fair value (¥2,080) alongside strong dividend yield and share repurchases.
